# Layout revision report — Riverside Park Plaza (60m x 40m, outdoor)

> This is a planning draft produced by an AI agent from simulation output. It is not a permit, fire-code or crowd-safety certification; a qualified reviewer must confirm it against the venue's actual conditions and applicable regulations.

## Summary

## Before / after

Identical conditions for every iteration: scenario `entry`, 200 agents, 300 s, seed 42, density grid 2 m (fingerprint `b2047e92`). Target: max density ≤ 2 p/m² with no validation errors.

| Metric | Baseline (iteration 0) | Final (iteration 1) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Max density | 3.27 p/m² | 2.25 p/m² | −1.02 p/m² (−31.2%) |
| p90 travel time | 175.8 s | 132.2 s | −43.6 s (−24.8%) |
| Mean travel time | 118.9 s | 95.7 s | −23.2 s (−19.5%) |
| Completed fraction | 99% | 100% | +1 pt |
| Hotspots | 3 | 1 | −2 |
| Validation errors | 0 | 0 | ±0 |

Stop reason: **no improvement** — max density 2.254 vs best so far 2.254 (0% < 2% required).

## Design brief (initial constraints)

Outdoor site: crowds spread less evenly than indoors and service access matters, so aisles are wider and every gate keeps a deeper clearance. The arrival plaza inside G-main stays open so queues and arriving visitors do not spill into the stalls. Food trucks (F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6) and the most popular stalls draw long queues, so they are kept away from the entrances. K1 sells tickets, so it sits beside G-main. The fire lane is unbuildable and must stay continuous; the engine enforces it.

- min_aisle_width 3 → 3.5 m
- door_clearance 5 → 6 m
- popular_threshold 0.8 → 0.7
- popular_door_distance 0 → 8 m
- open area in front of G-main: keep-out #1 added at (24, 0) 12×9 m
- K1 pinned at (22, 6.5) beside G-main

Booth coordinates were then computed by the layout solver under these constraints.

## What changed and why

**Revision after iteration 0 → 1.** High-attraction booths F3, F4, F5 sit in the entrance inflow; requiring popular booths to keep a distance from entrances separates arriving visitors from booth crowds.

- popular_door_distance 8 → 12 m

## Iteration history

| Iteration | Max density (p/m²) | p90 travel (s) | Completed | Errors | Comparable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 3.27 | 175.8 | 99% | 0 | yes |
| 1 | 2.25 | 132.2 | 100% | 0 | yes |
| 2 | 2.25 | 132.2 | 100% | 0 | yes |

## Assumptions

- Pedestrian metrics come from the **mock engine** (synthetic density field for demo purposes, not a pedestrian simulation); one scenario and seed per run, so results are a single sample, not a distribution.
- Booth popularity values are planning estimates of relative attraction, taken as given.
- Densities are peak values per grid cell over the run; hotspot thresholds are the engine's. Travel times count finished agents only.
- Geometric checks cover booth/obstacle/door-clearance/aisle rules only; egress capacity, fire code and accessibility were not assessed.
- Analysis and revision proposals by `stub`; all metrics and coordinates in this report are computed by tools.

## Unconfirmed items

- Ground slope and drainage not shown on site plan (from floor plan)
- Power hookup locations for food trucks unconfirmed (from floor plan)
- Rain contingency (tent weights / wind limits) not specified (from floor plan)
- Results not yet re-run on the real engine (OR-Tools layout, Shapely validation, JuPedSim)

---

# Layout revision report — Riverside Park Plaza (60m x 40m, outdoor)

Design brief: Outdoor site: crowds spread less evenly than indoors and service access matters, so aisles are wider and every gate keeps a deeper clearance. Food trucks (F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6) and the most popular stalls draw long queues, so they are kept away from the entrances. K1 sells tickets, so it sits beside G-main. The fire lane is unbuildable and must stay continuous; the engine enforces it. The solver placed the booths of Riverside Park Plaza (60m x 40m, outdoor) under those constraints and the layout was simulated under one fixed scenario. The worst congestion is hotspot #0. High-attraction booth F3, F4, F5 draws visitors into this zone.

Across 2 revisions it kept the layout as stable as possible and changed only what the simulation pointed at: High-attraction booths F3, F4, F5 sit in the entrance inflow; requiring popular booths to keep a distance from entrances separates arriving visitors from booth crowds; then Hotspot #0 persists next to F1, which shares the zone with other high-attraction booths; moving it south separates their visitor crowds. Each revised layout was re-validated and re-simulated with the identical scenario, so the before/after comparison below reflects layout changes only.
